source_quotes.exposures[0].device.manufacturer: As described in our previous paper [3], TUS was delivered using a 2-element spherically focusing annular array transducer (H115- 2AA, Sonic Concepts) with a nominal outer aperture diameter and radius of curvature of 64mm.

flags.reason: Paper does not describe the mechanism used to generate sham TUS pulses in this V1 study.
Stated duty cycle (50%) and PRF (250 Hz) imply a 2 ms pulse, but the stated total pulse duration is 3.25 ms (including a 1 ms Tukey ramp); recorded as stated, not recomputed.
Real TUS increased N75 VEP amplitude relative to no-TUS trials, but real vs sham TUS trials were not significantly different, leaving the auditory-confound-free effect unclear.

direction_notes: TUS alone did not evoke potentials in the TUS-only blocks. In the checkerboard blocks, the N75 VEP component amplitude was larger for real TUS than no-TUS trials, but there was no significant difference between real and sham TUS trials directly.

timing.protocol_description: Ramped pulses (1 ms Tukey ramp, 3.25 ms total pulse duration) were applied at a PRF of 250 Hz, with a pulse train duration of 300 ms and an effective duty cycle of 50%. In two TUS-only blocks, real and sham pulses (100 each) were applied randomly at a fixed inter-stimulus interval of 2 s; in two TUS checkerboard blocks, every fourth checkerboard flip (flipped every 0.5 s) was paired with a real or sham TUS trial (100 each), with the TUS trial starting 130 ms (±0-5 ms jitter) before the checkerboard flip.
